outcome: Rate of gestational weight gain above recommended range
cohort: The study included 7,543 women with singleton term pregnancies undergoing induction of labor with cervical dilatation at admission less than or equal to 3 cm, categorized by their BMI.
finding: Maternal obesity was identified as an independent factor associated with a significant increase in the rate of cesarean section in women undergoing induction of labor.
mod_finding: Compared with normal weight women, overweight and obese women undergoing induction of labor demonstrated a significantly higher rate of cesarean section (31.1% and 36.9% vs. 24.7%).
birth_weight: Macrosomia was observed in 15.0% of obese women vs. 11.1% of normal weight women.
gest_age: Term pregnancies (GA 39.7 ± 1.3 weeks for obese vs. 40.1 ± 1.3 weeks for normal weight women).
